title: Eighteen Days of War
subtitle: Research brief · full chapter in preparation
author: R.G. Cruise
summary: An assessment of the opening campaign and the limits of German success.
outlineTopics: The military situation after the opening eighteen days.
Army Group North's progress through the Baltic region.
Army Group Center's advances and the conclusion of the main Białystok–Minsk operation.
Army Group South's more difficult advance into Ukraine.
German operational successes and their limitations.
The condition of Soviet formations and continuing mobilization.
German and Soviet casualties and equipment losses, using carefully verified figures.
The status and treatment of Soviet prisoners of war.
German logistical problems and the growing distance from supply bases.
Occupation policies, atrocities, and mass shootings during the opening campaign.
The developing strategic importance of Smolensk.
The German expectation of Soviet collapse compared with the military situation actually emerging.
